practiceReport.name: Gracen Halton
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (DT) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
factors: Officially ruled Out on weekly game status report
practiceReport.beatComment: Halton sustained a broken left ankle in the fourth quarter, and he is now set to miss the rest of the 2026 campaign. With Halton unavailable, Osa Odighizuwa and DeForest Buckner will operate as San Francisco's primary options at defensive tackle moving forward.

practiceReport.name: Deebo Samuel Sr.
practiceReport.archetypeNote: High-contact YAC style; plays through upper-body pain tags (~86%) with extra caution on lower-body soft tissue.
factors: Questionable tag adjusted by player career prior (79%)

practiceReport.name: Demarcus Robinson
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
factors: Questionable tag adjusted by player career prior (76%)
practiceReport.beatComment: Robinson was carted off the field during the 49ers' Week 2 win against the Dolphins and was diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain, receiving a corresponding prognosis of 3-to-6 weeks on the sideline. After his placement on IR on Sept. 26, he missed the next five contests, but following a Week 8 bye, he was designated for return Wednesday and logged three straight limited sessions before being tagged as questionable. With his designation now a thing of the past, Robinson may immediately step into a prominent role in San Francisco's passing game Sunday due to fellow WRs Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) being out and Christian Kirk (knee) getting moved to IR.

practiceReport.name: Mike Evans
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran X-receiver toughness prior; routinely manages Wednesday reps but requires soft-tissue sprint clearance.
factors: Questionable tag adjusted by player career prior (84%)
practiceReport.beatComment: Evans is missing a second straight contest Sunday after aggravating a right Achilles injury during a Week 6 win against the Commanders. He hasn't been able to practice in the meantime, and while he's the type of player that doesn't require practice reps during the week to be available on game days, even work on the side Wednesday through Friday would be a welcome sign. In any case, with fellow WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring) also sidelined this weekend and Christian Kirk (knee) being placed on IR on Saturday, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing and KhaDarel Hodge are the options at the position to be active in Week 9.

practiceReport.name: Renardo Green
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (98% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
factors: Questionable tag adjusted by player career prior (82%)
practiceReport.beatComment: Green sustained the injury in the second half of the victory, and head coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game that the cornerback has not been ruled out for Week 10, suggesting that the injury is relatively minor. Green's status at practice will be worth monitoring when San Francisco returns to the field Wednesday, and if he can't play against the Cowboys on Nov. 15, Ephesians Prysock would be a top candidate to draw a start at cornerback.

practiceReport.name: Nick Bosa
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Regularly takes lighter Wednesday load; high active conversion once cleared for Thursday/Friday pass-rush reps.
practiceReport.beatComment: Bosa was sidelined for the 49ers' last five contests before their bye in Week 8 because of a nagging knee injury, but after an extra week of rest, he'll return to action in Week 9. He might not get his full regular workload right away, but he should play a significant role on the edge Sunday.

practiceReport.name: Luke Gifford
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (LB) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Gifford hurt his groin in Week 6 against Washington and didn't play in Week 7 versus Atlanta. However, San Francisco's Week 8 bye appears to have done him well, as the veteran linebacker returned to practice this week with an LP/LP/FP progression. Gifford has played primarily on special teams when healthy this season and will probably continue in that role against Las Vegas.

practiceReport.name: Marques Sigle
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Every-down starter workload (88% snaps) — 82% active conversion baseline when logging Limited Friday reps.
practiceReport.beatComment: Sigle missed the 49ers' last three games before their bye in Week 8 due to an ankle injury he sustained back in Week 4 versus the Broncos, but he's now set to get back on the field in Week 9. He projects to start at safety next to Ji'Ayir Brown against Las Vegas on Sunday.

practiceReport.name: Garret Wallow
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (LB) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Wallow was sidelined due to a strained hamstring in Weeks 6 and 7, but San Francisco's Week 8 bye gave him some extra recovery time. With an LP/LP/FP practice progression under his belt this week, the veteran linebacker is set to return to action against the Raiders. Wallow typically plays less than a quarter of the 49ers' defensive snaps, so he's not a recommended IDP option in fantasy.

practiceReport.name: Deommodore Lenoir
practiceReport.archetypeNote: High snap durability across boundary and slot corner alignments.
factors: Questionable tag adjusted by player career prior (92%)
practiceReport.beatComment: Lenoir notched three solo tackles, one of which was for a loss, in the contest, but he didn't leave unscathed. Head coach Kyle Shanahan explained after the game that the cornerback hasn't been ruled out for Week 10, suggesting that Lenoir may have avoided a major injury. If he is forced to miss any action moving forward, Ashtyn Davis and Ephesians Prysock are both candidates to see increased workload in the secondary.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Nate Hobbs
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 8 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Hobbs had his practice window opened Wednesday and logged three limited practices before initially being deemed questionable to face the Raiders on Sunday. Since he wasn't activated Saturday, the veteran cornerback will have to wait at least another week to return to action. Hobbs' next chance to do so is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Dallas.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Christian Kirk
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Kirk made his season debut in San Francisco's last game in Week 7 in Atlanta, going without a target on a 30 percent snap share. After a Week 8 bye, he showed up on the initial Week 9 practice report Wednesday as limited due to a knee injury, which head coach Kyle Shanahan revealed to be to the wide receiver's meniscus Friday, per David Lombardi of SFStandard.com. Shanahan also relayed that Robinson may need surgery, but at the very least he'll miss the team's next four contests.

irAndReserveTracker.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Stribling, who garnered his share of preseason fantasy buzz, was injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams, but it appears as though the wideout is making solid progress in his recovery. A firm timetable for the 2026 second-rounder's return to practice hasn't been outlined yet, but David Lombardi of SFStandard.com previously noted that Stribling (ankle) remains on track to return at some point in December, a notion supported by Barrows' report.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Sam Okuayinonu
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday he hopes Okuayinonu can return near the end of the regular season, but it is unclear quite how long the recovery process will take. Okuayinonu previously had a plate in his foot, and the break occurred when it was stepped on during practice.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Austen Pleasants
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Pleasants sustained a knee injury during the 49ers' preseason game against the Chargers on Aug. 20. The injury is severe enough for 29-year-old offensive tackle to open the year on IR, meaning he'll be forced to miss at least the first four games of the regular season.

irAndReserveTracker.name: C.J. West
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: It remains unclear what issue is sidelining the second-year player. West will now need to miss at least four games on IR before becoming eligible to return to the active roster. The defensive tackle has logged five tackles (one solo) over 49 defensive snaps in the 49ers' first two regular-season games.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Isaac Guerendo
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Guerendo spent all of training camp on the active/PUP list and is seemingly not ready to take the field, so he will remain on PUP and will miss at least the first four weeks of the season. As such, Kaelon Black and Jordan James will open as the top two options behind starter Christian McCaffrey (undisclosed).

irAndReserveTracker.name: Nick Martin
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Martin opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a hamstring injury that he sustained during training camp in August. Shanahan said Martin is "getting close" to returning to practice, and if he's cleared for field work this week, his participation level will shed light on whether he'll play in Week 6 against the Commanders on Monday, Oct. 19. The 2025 third-rounder logged 11 tackles (eight solo) and one fumble recovery across seven regular-season games during his rookie campaign, which he finished on injured reserve due to a concussion.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Brandon Aiyuk
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Reserve/Left Squad — requires formal NFL & club reinstatement
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Per Wagoner, Aiyuk submitted paperwork to be reinstated to the NFL in late October, and since then both the NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association have been involved in an attempt to reach a resolution that's agreeable to both the wide receiver and the 49ers. Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Thursday that Aiyuk's efforts to secure his release may be hampered by the roughly $13 million in bonus forfeitures that he owes the team, which could mean arbitration comes into play and delays the process. Friday's meeting between Aiyuk, his agent Drew Rosenhaus and San Francisco brass was only the first step. If the sides reach an agreement, the 49ers will have three options: release Aiyuk, trade him before Tuesday's deadline or add him to their 53-man roster.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Alfred Collins
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: This move was anticipated, as Collins is set to miss the entire 2026 campaign as a result of tearing his patellar tendon during practice Tuesday. Osa Odighizuwa, CJ West and Gracen Halton should get plenty of reps at defensive tackle with Collins and Sam Okuayinonu (foot) sidelined.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Andrew Farmer II
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Farmer was not picked up by another squad after the 49ers waived him with an injury designation earlier in the week, and now he'll be required to stay on the team's IR list for the year unless he negotiates an injury settlement. He last played regular-season snaps in 2023 with the Chargers.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Darrick Forrest
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: It's not clear what kind of injury Forrest is dealing with, but he's now on track to spend the entire 2026 season on IR unless he negotiates an injury settlement with the 49ers. His absence could open up more opportunities for rookie undrafted free agents Jalen Stroman and Larry Worth.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jake Tonges
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The team placed Tonges on injured reserve earlier Wednesday, and now it's official that he will miss the rest of the season. Tonges suffered an MCL tear in the season opener against the Rams. Jack Stoll was signed to the practice squad to add depth, and Luke Farrell now projects to be the second tight end behind George Kittle.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Mikail Kamara
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Placed on Injured Reserve (Knee) on Aug 3, 2026; ineligible to return in 2026 under NFL CBA rules.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Nick Zakelj
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The nature of Zakelj's injury is unclear, as is when he exactly picked up the injury. However, by being placed on IR without a designation to return, the 2022 sixth-rounder will be forced to miss the entire upcoming season unless he reached an injury settlement with San Francisco.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Ricky Pearsall
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: The procedure typically carries a wide-ranging recovery timeline of 6-to-12 months, so while Pearsall will be ruled out for the season, it's not clear if he'll be available for the start of the 49ers' offseason program next spring or the start of training camp next summer. The wideout will wind up having played in just 20 of a possible 51 regular-season contests and one of two playoff games through his first three NFL campaigns, missing time as a rookie while recovering from a gunshot wound to the chest before being hampered by the PCL injury off and on in 2025. He'll turn 27 in September and will be entering the final season of his rookie contract in 2027.
